Detail: Search pending zoning, permits, and agenda items by topic within a radius. Same pattern serves warehouses, rezoning, road projects.
Notes: 2026-08-18 (g19 item 6). BUILT AS THE GENERAL SHAPE, not a data-center feature: lib/routing/agenda-search.ts carries EIGHT topics - data centers, warehouses and distribution centres, rezonings, road projects, housing developments, cell towers, solar and wind, school closures - and adding 'is there a landfill coming' is adding words to AGENDA_TOPICS, not writing code. Phrases are multi-word by preference, because 'center' is a community centre and a senior centre and a recreation centre and one loose word makes the reader filter the noise for us; the longest matching phrase wins so 'distribution center' is not claimed by a shorter entry inside it. NOTHING GENERATES. The answer is the clerk's own agenda line, quoted verbatim with the phrase that matched it named, and the document linked beside it - a generated summary of a zoning agenda is a claim about what a government is about to do, made by us, and the line the clerk typed is better evidence and already there. Served by POST /api/ask/agenda because the corpus is 140 documents of extracted text and shipping it to a browser to answer one question trades the reader's bandwidth for our convenience; it stores nothing, logs nothing, keeps no IP. THE SCOPE IS DIVISIONS, NOT DISTANCE, and that is a deviation from the row's wording recorded rather than hidden: meetingsWithin() exists and the route takes a point, but a rezoning in YOUR town is your business whether the town hall is two miles off or thirty, and a county board thirty miles away decides more of your street than a neighbouring city's council does at five. So the client sends the divisions it already has - the same approximate-location basis the search log uses - and the response says which scope it used, because 'we found nothing' means different things in each. VERIFIED LIVE against a dev server at Pima's divisions: 2 hits of 15 readable agendas with 9 unreadable stated separately, and the second hit is 'Establishing a 120-day Moratorium on Data Centers in Unincorporated Pima County' - the reader's exact question answered out of the county's own agenda. Across the whole corpus: 56 hits over 8 topics, 122 readable documents of 140. A document whose extraction FAILED is counted as unreadable and never as an agenda with nothing on it - our parsing failure must not become a claim about a government. THE ONE-DEFINITION RULE HELD: an agenda hit is an ANSWER, so askWasAnswered() was EXTENDED to take the hit count rather than the component growing a second opinion beside it - g11's defect exactly, and tests/ask-matcher.test.ts now refuses an OR at the call site as well as pinning the call. The refusal render reads the same extended definition, so a reader with a real agenda answer is never told underneath it that we have no sourced answer. 9 tests in tests/ask-agenda.test.ts, against the committed corpus rather than a fixture, asserting minimum counts and that every quote is findable verbatim in the document it is attributed to. STILL OPEN: permits and zoning-application data proper (this searches AGENDAS, which is where those items surface but is not the permit record itself), and the corpus is only as wide as the agenda retrieval cap. BUILT ON THE NIGHTLY BULK CSV, NOT THE v3 API: data.openstates.org/people/current/<st>.csv, one file per state, NO KEY AND NO LOGIN REQUIRED, verified live for az/nj/nh (200, 84KB/119KB/354KB). So PLURAL_API_KEY is NOT needed for the roster - it is for the API, which this does not touch. Data is CC-0; attribution is requested not required and is carried anyway. 620 legislators fetched. THE NEW HAMPSHIRE TRAP, and it is the at-large trap again in a different costume. Plural designates NH House districts by county and number - "Merrimack 8", "Rockingham 30" - while this repo identifiers are Census numeric codes, sldl:608. A direct join scores 0 OF 201 and does so silently. The bridge is the registry own Census-sourced LABEL, which carries the statutory designation: sldl:608 is labelled "State House District Merrimack 08". indexDivisions() keys on state|chamber|normalized-designation and designationKey() strips zero-padding so "Merrimack 08" meets "Merrimack 8". This is NOT the name-string join CLAUDE.md forbids: that rule is about joining geographic entities on colloquial names that collide across states, whereas a NH House district designation IS its statutory identity, the match is scoped to one state and one chamber, it is exact after normalization rather than fuzzy, and every miss is reported. Output is keyed on this repo OCD-IDs throughout. RESULT, and the denominator matters: AZ 90 legislators / 24 linked, NJ 120 / 21, NH 410 / 85. The apparent shortfall is the THREE-COUNTY CLIP, not a mismatch - the registry holds 16 AZ, 14 NJ and 53 NH legislative districts, and ALL OF THEM now have someone. Zero holes. The build prints held-vs-covered per state precisely so a clip is never mistaken for a broken join. MANY-TO-MANY CONFIRMED IN REAL DATA: AZ LD19 returns one senator (David Gowan) and TWO representatives (Gail Griffin, Lupe Diaz); NJ Assembly District 25 returns two Assemblymembers; NH Merrimack 07 returns two. A one-district-per-seat column would have had to drop half of them. CHAMBER TITLES ARE A PER-STATE TABLE, not derived: NJ lower chamber is the General Assembly and its members are Assemblymembers, not Representatives. A state with no entry reports rather than inventing a title, same rule as the body registry refusing to mint supervisors/commissioners/select boards. STILL MISSING: term dates (the CSV carries none - needs the API or the openstates/people YAML), and photos (Plural publishes an image URL; not shipped because it would be a hotlink of unknown licence - D20). QUOTA RECORDED 2026-08-12, branch claude/plural-quota-and-vendor-note, test (132 pass) lint build all green. Plural free tier is 500 GraphQL requests/day at 1 req/sec. THIS IS A QUOTA, NOT A TERMS RESTRICTION - it limits how we build, not whether we may, so D03 STAYS CLEARED. It is also the reason the bulk route is correct rather than merely preferred: 620 legislators across AZ/NJ/NH under any per-person or per-district GraphQL pattern would spend most of a day allowance in one build and do it again on every rerun. The bulk route costs 3 static requests, metered against nothing. The build now PRINTS both counters separately every run - "requests: 3 bulk (unmetered) / 0 GraphQL of 500/day" - and warns above 50% of the ceiling, so the limit is a visible number rather than something discovered by hitting a 429. Counters are kept apart deliberately: adding static bulk downloads to the GraphQL count would invent pressure on a ceiling nothing is near. tests/plural.test.ts gained a regression guard asserting bulkUrl points at data.openstates.org and NOT at the API host, because the likely way this breaks is someone reaching for GraphQL to fill in term dates, which the CSV lacks. If GraphQL is ever needed: serialize at 1 req/sec, cache hard, never re-fetch unchanged, print the count. Written up in docs/vendor-review.md as a fourth section, framed as the different kind of entry it is - Plural PUBLISHES public-domain data rather than holding a public body records, so there is no access question of the sort Granicus/Hyland/Diligent raise, and CC-0 means it is the only source in that document with no commercial-use question at all. || 2026-08-17 TYPO CORRECTION TO THE AUTHOR'S DISPOSITION, recorded so the session that builds this works from the right list. Item: clerksboards parser reads past published month restrictions and exceptions
Detail: Three of Tucson's 27 wired Clerk boards publish a schedule the parser expands more broadly than the body wrote it. Board 40: '2nd Tuesday of each month September through May @ 6:00 p.m.' - the September-through-May restriction is ignored, so June, July and August sittings would be emitted. Boards 58 and 59: '1st Thursday of each month @ 9:00 a.m. (except January it will be 01/08/26 and July will be 07/09/26)' - the parenthetical exception is ignored, so those two months get the ordinary Nth-weekday date instead of the published one. Neither produces a wrong date inside today's serving window, because the recurrence loop only walks five months ahead from the window start; both will as soon as the window or the loop widens. This is one class, not three instances: the grammar has no representation for a restriction or an exception attached to a recurrence. Found 2026-08-18 (g19) by re-running the classification over all 56 board pages, and recorded rather than fixed under the addition rule.
Notes: Opened 2026-08-18 (g19 item 1b). The fix has a shape already: monthsInParens() in lib/sources/clerksboards/index.ts reads a month set out of a parenthetical for grammar C, and the same helper is what a restriction clause needs. The exception form is different - it is a date OVERRIDE for a named month, so the recurrence has to be expanded first and then patched, which is why it is not a one-line change. A test must assert the negative (no June/July/August date for board 40) as well as the positive, because the current window hides the defect and a test written against today's window would pass on a broken parser.

Item: A data-fetch script overwrote verified data with less of it, and reported success
Detail: 2026-08-18 (g19), caught and reverted in-session. A new key-votes resolver was written on the brief's statement that votes on laws was unbuilt, and run against data/votes/key-votes-snapshot.json without re-reading it first. The snapshot already carried 18 of 20 law entries with both chambers verified. The run resolved the four April 2024 siblings to their Senate VEHICLE - which carries no House vote of its own - and wrote that over four correct House roll calls; House coverage went 18 to 15 and the run printed 'LAWS carrying at least one roll call: 18/20', which was true and which hid the loss entirely, because the entries still had their Senate refs. It took a same-session diff against git HEAD to see it. Two things went wrong and they are separable: a stale docblock made a false premise survive, and a merge that replaced rather than compared made the consequence silent.
Notes: Opened 2026-08-18 (g19 item 4). MITIGATED, NOT CLOSED. Three things landed with it: the resolver's merge is now non-destructive by construction (a run may add refs and may never remove one, and a refusal to shrink is counted and PRINTED, so a run that declined to improve anything and a run that improved everything cannot print the same line); tests/key-votes.test.ts pins law coverage as a floor that only rises, so this specific loss now fails a gate rather than shipping; and lib/votes/key-votes.ts's stale docblock was corrected. WHAT IS STILL OPEN is the general shape, which is not specific to votes: every fetch script in scripts/ that rewrites a committed artifact can do this, and most report a total that stays flat while a component of it falls. The general fix is a per-artifact floor - a script that writes fewer rows, fewer matched keys, or fewer non-null fields than the file it is replacing must refuse and say so, the way lib/meetings/snapshot.ts already refuses a snapshot whose sources do not state integer counts. A sweep of the fetch scripts against that rule is the work. Related and already-standing: the refresh corollary (a failed fetch never silently empties a previously-full surface) is the same rule one layer up, and this is that rule applied to a SUCCESSFUL fetch that simply found less.

Item: Montana's district count does not reconcile between NCES and the Census of Governments
Detail: NCES CCD reports 387 regular open school districts for Montana. The 2022 Census of Governments reports 311 independent school districts for Montana, with ZERO dependent school systems to account for the gap. Every other large state-level gap in the Census/CCD comparison resolves once dependent systems are added back; Montana does not, and it is the only unreconciled variance in the set. 76 districts, unexplained. NOT URGENT, and BLOCKING before any Montana-specific or state-level school-district coverage claim: the official-universe rule requires a coverage claim to be measured against the Census of Governments and NCES rather than against our own registry's count, and that rule assumes the two agree, or that dependent systems reconcile them. Montana is the case where neither holds, so 'we watch N of M districts in Montana' has no defensible M until this is settled.
Notes: Opened 2026-08-18 (g19 item 10, the author's order). Nothing was run and nothing is claimed about Montana. The likely shapes to check, none of them assumed: NCES counts operating LEAs including ones the Census treats as dependent on a county or a municipality even where the state-level dependent count reads zero; Montana's elementary and high-school districts are separately chartered and may be counted once by one and twice by the other; and the two use different reference years, so a district created or dissolved between them shows as a variance that is really a date difference. Whichever it is, the answer has to come from the two agencies' own definitions rather than from splitting the difference. Related: docs/coverage-audit-by-county.md holds the per-county audit this denominator feeds.

Item: Two scheduled workflows push to main with no rebase, so a collision loses a run
Detail: intake-tripwire.yml and refresh-meetings-snapshot.yml both commit and 'git push origin main' with no pull, rebase or retry. When both run close together the second push is rejected 'fetch first' and the job fails red after doing all of its work correctly.
Notes: FOUND 2026-08-18 (g13) while verifying R43 and R44: both workflows were dispatched at once to prove the two fixes, the tripwire pushed its report first, and the meetings refresh - whose ingest, whose M59 gate and whose commit had all SUCCEEDED - failed on the push alone. Re-dispatched by itself it passed, which is the proof the failure was the race and not the work. The scheduled cadences make this uncommon rather than impossible (17 past every sixth hour against 41 past ten), and a run lost this way is not silent - it goes red - so this is a P2. THE FIX IS SMALL AND SHOULD BE CONSIDERED WHOLE RATHER THAN PATCHED TWICE: a pull --rebase before the push, or a short retry loop, applied to BOTH workflows in one edit, since a fix on one only moves which job loses. Note the failure mode it must not create: a rebase that silently drops the commit would turn a red run into a green one that changed nothing, which is the empty success CLAUDE.md forbids - so the retry has to verify the push landed and stay red if it did not.
